entries.description: Operator set pathAwareCritique: advisory.
Register.

**Fix the TypeScript synthesizer.** `utils/sessionState.ts::buildSessions` hardcodes ``title: `Session ${n}` `` while the same module already imports and calls `extractSessionTitlesFromSpec`. Thread the map it already computes into the loop, applying the same resolution order the Python writer documents. **No new file read** — if the change adds one, it is the wrong change.

**Settle the sticky-generic problem, which is the actual bug.** Because resolution puts the existing ledger first, a `"Session N"` already on disk is carried forward by every boundary write and never heals. Decide and test the rule: a spec heading beats a **generic-shaped** stored title (`Session <own number>`), while a genuinely operator-authored title is still never overwritten. Every existing set must end up healed without a migration script.

**Settle which `ensureSessionStateFile` owns lazy synthesis.** Two writers — `ai_router/session_state.py` and `utils/sessionState.ts` — currently create the same file, and the extension's watcher makes the race real and observable. Record the ownership decision where writer discipline is documented; a Python↔TypeScript parity test for title resolution is the enforcement (precedent: the menu-parity test, and `sessionStepModel`'s regex, which is explicitly maintained as a mirror).
Full pytest and the Layer 2 tree-provider harness at close after freeze; verify, close.
Register: start_session recorded session 1 in flight
Fix the TypeScript synthesizer: buildSessions threads the spec title map it already computed, through the shared healTitle rule
Settle the sticky-generic problem: a spec heading beats a generic-shaped stored title, at the writer AND in the read view so closed sets heal without a migration script
Settle lazy-synthesis ownership: the router writes, the extension read derives in memory; parity corpus + both halves shipped
Verification: discovery (2 lenses) + supplementary found 3 Major, all remediated; remediation-review returned VERIFIED with 2 fix-accepted verdicts
Register.

**Add a session-scoped reveal**: activating a session node opens `spec.md` and reveals/selects that session's `### Session N of M:` block. Left-click on a **set** row already opens `spec.md` (`dabblerSessionSets.openSpec` via `planLeftClickActivation`) — this is the session-level sibling of a behaviour that exists, so reuse the plumbing rather than adding a parallel one.
**Degrade to the truth.** A malformed or missing heading opens `spec.md` at the top rather than erroring or showing nothing. The operator always ends up looking at the real file.

**Keep the decision honest about scope**: if the plain reveal reads as too unfocused when actually used, record that finding — a read-only virtual document on a custom scheme is the sanctioned next step, and it is a *recorded* decision with a reason, not a default.
Full Layer 3 at close after freeze; verify, close.
Registered session 2 via start_session; preload read (constitution, project-guidance, lessons-learned, AGENTS.md); transport profile copilot-cli confirmed.

Session rows now carry dabblerWorkExplorer.activateSession, which dispatches the EXISTING dabblerSessionSets.openSpec with the session node; openSpec reveals the section via the new pure providers/specSectionLocator.ts (borrowing sessionStepModel.scanSessionHeads so one regex decides what a session heading is). Layer 2 green: 13 new assertions.

Every unanswerable case (no session number, unreadable spec, no matching heading, spec ahead of the ledger, EISDIR) returns undefined and opens spec.md at the top; the reveal itself falls back to vscode.open on any throw. Proven at Layer 2 (6 cases) and in a real host: a heading-less fixture opens at Ln 1 with no notification toast.

Journaled two decisions: (a) one command, two callers - openSpec takes an optional section, heading scan borrowed from sessionStepModel rather than re-derived; (b) the plain reveal ships as showTextDocument + revealRange(AtTop) with an empty selection, and whether it reads as focused enough is tagged uat_decide for the set walk - no custom scheme on this evidence, per the spec non-goal.
Targeted runs recorded: Layer 2 full 1721 passing / 1 pending; new Layer 3 spec 2/2 in a real host. Full Layer 3 run of record is taken at close after the last code change.

Runs of record after the last code change: mocha 1721 passing / 1 pending (49s), playwright 38 passed (14.1m, includes the 2 new session-plan-reveal scenarios). pytest fresh from S1 - no ai_router source changed. Verification VERIFIED (gpt-5.5, both discovery lenses, 0 blocking findings, 1 nit).
Register.

**Add session-scoped context-menu actions** through the existing `ActionRegistry` and the `contextValue` vocabulary the session node already carries (`workExplorerTreeModel` emits `session-<status>` tokens), so menu parity stays enforced by the existing parity test rather than by hand.

**Copy the run prompt for that session.** Session-scoped sibling of the set-level L5 clipboard shortcut, and of the existing builders in `commands/copyPromptCommands.ts`. Gate on status the way `planLeftClickActivation` does — and **fail closed on an unrecognised status**, as that helper deliberately does.

**Open the artifacts for that session** — QuickPick when there is more than one, reusing the `openSpec` plumbing the registry already notes for this case. **Discover them by convention (`s<N>-*`), never by a hardcoded list**, so the menu survives artifact churn; show an honest empty state when a session has produced nothing yet.
Full Layer 3 at close after freeze; verify, close.

Registered session 3 via start_session (github-copilot / anthropic / claude-opus-5, effort high); preload read; Copilot CLI transport confirmed via ai_router/local-overrides.yaml, so no provider API keys are required; decision-review queue empty; prerequisites from S1 (title fix, parity test) and S2 (specSectionLocator, activateSession) confirmed on disk.

Added SESSION_ACTIONS to providers/ActionRegistry.ts (a separate list, because a session action reads the session and every existing RowAction reads only the set) and taught sessionDescriptor to emit their tokens through the same actionToken/tokenString seam the set row uses. package.json gains two commands, two commandPalette hides and two view/item/context entries in a new 6_session group. The Set 110 S2 assertion that no menu entry targets a session row is SUPERSEDED BY DECISION rather than deleted: it now covers bucket and step rows, and a new Set 115 S3 parity suite asserts the replacement rule (each session action appears exactly once as a top-level item, gates on its own delimited token, mints no token a set action owns, is hidden from the palette, and is never inline).

Added dabbler.copySessionRunPrompt. The pure gate is rowMenuHelpers.nextRunnableSessionNumber + sessionOffersRunPrompt: the set-level half BORROWS planLeftClickActivation (so the set row and the session row cannot drift on what a runnable set is), and the session-level half walks the ledger in ascending order, skips complete/cancelled, and fails closed on the first unrecognised status - the ~10 percent mis-spelled status tokens step-ledger-findings.md measured are exactly the input that would otherwise nominate the wrong session. Only the row the trigger phrase resolves to carries the prompt, and the text is buildStartNextSessionPrompt verbatim, so no new trigger-phrase vocabulary is minted (decisions.jsonl D1). The command re-checks the gate on dispatch, because contextValue is computed at render time.

Added dabblerSessionSets.openSessionArtifacts. Discovery is by convention (isSessionArtifact / listSessionArtifacts in commands/openFile.ts): case-insensitive ^s<N>-. on the top-level files of the set dir, sorted, so s3- cannot swallow s30- and a new artifact shape needs no code change. One match opens directly, several open a QuickPick (the openPrerequisiteSpec shape), none produces a message naming the session, the set and the s<N>-* convention. The entry is offered unconditionally and answered on the CLICK, because hiding it would need a readdir per session row on the tree scan (decisions.jsonl D2). Layer 2 coverage in sessionRowActions.test.ts (41 assertions green with the parity suite), Layer 3 in session-menu.spec.ts.
